title: New experts join Google’s AI & Economy team
gist: Google is expanding its AI & Economy Research Program with Nobel laureate economist Philippe Aghion, Ajay Agrawal, and new co-directors Anu Madgavkar (ex-McKinsey Global Institute) and Daniel Rock (Wharton), pairing outside academic credibility with Google's own frontier-model usage telemetry to become an authoritative source on AI's labor and productivity effects.

themes.theme: Proprietary telemetry as a research edge

insights.claim: Google is building internal research capacity to empirically measure AI's economic impact on jobs, productivity, and growth using its own tool-usage data (via the AI & Economy ATLAS) and frontier-model telemetry, rather than relying solely on external academic studies.
insights.speaker: Scott Strand
insights.so_what: Positions Google as a gatekeeper of ground-truth data on AI's economic effects, which could shape policy narratives and its own regulatory positioning.
insights.locator: We recently launched the AI & Economy ATLAS v1.0

insights.claim: Incoming co-director Daniel Rock (Wharton) will 'bridge frontier model telemetry with rigorous econometrics' to study enterprise productivity and labor restructuring, implying Google will grant its economics team access to granular internal data on how enterprises actually use its frontier AI models.
insights.speaker: Scott Strand
insights.so_what: Data access unavailable to independent academics gives Google a research edge, but also means findings from this program should be read as coming from a data-advantaged, self-interested party.
insights.quote: bridging frontier model telemetry with rigorous econometrics to analyze enterprise productivity, labor restructuring, and scientific discovery
insights.locator: Daniel Rock: Joining from the Wharton School

insights.claim: Google recruited 2025 Nobel laureate economist Philippe Aghion, known for his work on innovation-led growth and creative destruction, as an academic advisor to help model AI's long-term macroeconomic trajectory, joining existing advisors Nobel laureate Michael Spence and Cambridge economist Diane Coyle.
insights.speaker: Scott Strand
insights.so_what: High-profile economist recruitment signals Google expects AI's macroeconomic narrative to be a major battleground and wants first-mover framing power over how that story is told.

insights.claim: New co-director Anu Madgavkar, formerly a Partner at the McKinsey Global Institute with two decades leading global research on labor markets and technology adoption, will lead Google's empirical research on global AI diffusion, small-business ecosystems, and generative AI's workforce impact.
insights.speaker: Scott Strand
insights.so_what: Google appears to be building capacity to produce influential 'future of work' style research comparable to MGI's, positioning itself as a primary source on AI labor-market diffusion.

insights.claim: Ajay Agrawal will join as a Visiting Fellow collaborating closely with MIT's David Autor, and the program frames his work explicitly as advancing 'how AI can expand the frontier of human welfare' rather than using purely productivity-centric language.
insights.speaker: Scott Strand
insights.so_what: The welfare-economics framing (versus pure productivity framing) hints at the policy narrative Google intends to promote around AI's societal benefit, useful context for anticipating Google's public communication on AI and labor.
insights.quote: how AI can expand the frontier of human welfare

insights.claim: Google's AI & Economy Research Program organizes its work around four core areas: the future of work, productivity and growth, global technology diffusion, and AI's impact on scientific discovery.
insights.speaker: Scott Strand
insights.so_what: This framework previews the categories investors and policymakers should expect to see repeatedly in Google's future AI-economy reporting and ATLAS updates.
insights.quote: focusing on core areas including the future of work, productivity and growth, global technology diffusion, and AI’s impact on scientific discovery
insights.locator: Our program measures and analyzes this evolution in real time
